newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Volatility play in Office Depot.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Volatility play in Office Depot.

text.p: A professional trading firm made a sizable volatility play on Office Depot Inc, using the July call options, traders said Friday.

By 1130 CDT/1630 GMT, the Office Depot July 10 call traded 2,100 contracts, the July 12-1/2 call traded 1,475, the July 15 call traded 1,595, the July 17-1/2 call traded 3,130 and the July 20 call traded 2,590.
"It was a professional order," said Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners. "It was done for the customer selling volatility."
He said the trading crowd took the other side of the trade.
Office Depot shares were up 1/8 at 14-1/4.

In early April, federal regulators moved to block the office superstore's proposed merger with Staples Inc, but Office Depot said last week it still thought the merger was in the best interests of its customers and shareholders.
Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said the investor doing the volatility play may be expecting volatility to drop to pre-merger levels.
Volatilities in the active July options were in the 70 to 80 region.
Schwartz said historical volatility was high, boosted by a level of 136 in March.
"Pre-merger, the volatility was in the range of 30, so he could possibly be expecting it to go back to pre-merger volatility levels," he said.
He explained the investor most likely bought the in-the-money options, the 10s and 12-1/2s, and sold the out-of-the moneys.
He said volatility on the out-of-the-money calls could come down even if the stock trades flat.
The investor would then be able to buy those options back at lower prices, keeping the difference as profit.
"If the stock closes within certain parameters, he makes money," Schwarz at AGS Specialist Partners added.
Oppenheimer's Schwartz said the investor's risk on the long call position was 5/8.
"So if the stock stays the same, he's got 5/8 risk on that position, but he could make the premium on the 17-1/2s, 20s and even the 15s if he sold that one," he said.
The Office Depot July 15 calls were trading at two, the 17-1/2 calls at 1-1/16 and the 20 calls at 1/2.
"He's long the in-the-moneys and short the out-of-the-moneys to take advantage of a potential adjustment in the volatility," he said.

In other trading, volatilities in options on Philip Morris Cos Inc and RJR Nabisco Holdings remained high as the underlying stocks fell after a federal judge ruled that the Food and Drug Administration can regulate sales and labeling on cigarettes but cannot regulate the promotion and advertising of tobacco products, Schwarz said.
